notes.1ai: Most of the correct answers seen used a slotted mass with ‘5’ seen in the hole.
notes.1aii: This was answered well by the majority of candidates.
notes.1b: Most candidates correctly calculated the value b / a to the required, and consistent, number of decimal places.
notes.1c: Almost all candidates labelled the axes with the correct quantity and unit, with appropriate scales and plots. Candidates should ensure that the plots on the graph are precise and not blobs, with crosses being an acceptable alternative. Most candidates drew a good well-judged line.
notes.1di: Evidence of how the gradient was determined was seen from many candidates.
notes.1dii: Only stronger candidates stated a correct value and unit.
notes.1e: This was answered quite well with a variety of correct responses.
notes.2a: (b) Most candidates obtained a correct set of experimental results.
notes.2c: Most candidates stated their results to correct and consistent decimal places.
notes.2dii: Many candidates gained partial credit for matching their statement to their results but then did not justify it by referring to either that they were within a suitable percentage experimental error or by quoting numerical values.
notes.2ei: Many candidates identified the advantage of using a variable resistor.
notes.2eii: Quite a few candidates did not know the correct symbol.
notes.2f: Many candidates recognised that a straight line was required here.
notes.3a: Most candidates correctly drew the normal and the line NA .
notes.3b: Many candidates used sufficient pin separation in their work.
notes.3c: The ray lines were usually correctly drawn.
notes.3di: (ii) Most candidates correctly drew the line and measured the angle.
notes.3diii: Only a few correct statements were seen and very few justifications were given.
notes.3e: The most common answers seen were “thin lines / sharp pencil” or “ensure pins far apart”.
notes.3f: There were very few clear answers seen.
